leaf.displayName: Leaf Green (reserved: confirm, not yet applied)

display.purpose: The game name in the pelmet; white fill over a 5px ink keyline painted first (4px when short).

headline.purpose: Big top-bar numerals; 24px at heights of 500px and below.

body.purpose: All running text; tabular numerals; 60ch max in cards.

label.purpose: Tiny uppercase tracked caps over numerals, in blush on curtain; 10px when short.

keycap.purpose: Key letters inside hint chips, royal blue.

shadows.name: paper-lift
shadows.purpose: The only UI shadow: lifts floating card pieces (camera buttons, key chips, notice) off the stage. No hard offset block shadows.

shadows.name: world-sun
shadows.value: Three.js DirectionalLight #ffffff intensity 1.35 at (-10, 20, 12), PCF soft shadow map 2048, bias -0.0006; AmbientLight #ffffff 2.1
shadows.purpose: Real soft shadows in the diorama. Day-cycle light shift (warm dusk, dim night) is planned, not built.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for all UI state transitions.

motion.name: meter-slide
motion.purpose: Loved/Feared thumb moving to a new position.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion, meter and buttons snap.

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.purpose: Phones held sideways: 56px pelmet, 16px scallops, tighter type ramp.

breakpoints.name: coarse
breakpoints.purpose: Hides camera turn buttons and key hints (camera turning is a PC extra).

outlines.name: world-ink
outlines.purpose: Diorama edges: grass rim and wooden base.

outlines.name: focus
outlines.purpose: Keyboard focus on every focusable element; the map shows a 4px marigold frame below the pelmet instead.

components.name: Pelmet
components.description: Curtain-red valance with a scalloped ink-edged hem holding the crest and big-number stats.
components.css: .ds-pelmet { position: relative; height: 76px; padding: 0 24px; margin-bottom: 25px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 36px; background: #c8324a; border-bottom: 3px solid #3b2a2e; color: #fff; } .ds-pelmet::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: -25px; height: 22px; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 0, #c8324a 17px, #3b2a2e 17px 20px, transparent 20.5px) 0 0 / 48px 22px; background-repeat: round no-repeat; } .ds-crest { font: 400 30px/1 'Lilita One', 'Nunito', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.01em; -webkit-text-stroke: 5px #3b2a2e; paint-order: stroke fill; } .ds-stats { display: flex; gap: 28px; margin: 0; } .ds-stat { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; } .ds-stat dt { font: 800 11px/1 'Nunito', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #fff2f4; } .ds-stat dd { margin: 0; font: 400 32px/1.05 'Lilita One', sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Loved/Feared Meter
components.description: Flat Loved/Feared halves with an ink tick at even and a white card thumb.
components.css: .ds-meter { --pos: 50%; position: relative; display: block; width: 170px; height: 14px; margin: 12px; border: 3px solid #3b2a2e; border-radius: 9px; background: linear-gradient(#3b2a2e, #3b2a2e) 50% 0 / 3px 100% no-repeat, linear-gradient(90deg, #f59ac0 50%, #2f5fa8 50%); } .ds-meter::after { content: ""; position: absolute; top: -7px; left: calc(var(--pos) - 6px); width: 12px; height: 22px; background: #fffdf8; border: 3px solid #3b2a2e; border-radius: 4px; transition: left 400ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); }

components.name: Camera Turn Button
components.description: Round printed-card icon button with ink line icon; PC extra, hidden on coarse pointers.
components.html: <button type="button" class="ds-turn" aria-label="Turn camera left"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 12a7 7 0 1 0 2.1-5" /><path d="M7.5 2.5 7.1 7l4.4.6" /></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-turn { width: 52px; height: 52px; display: grid; place-items: center; padding: 0; border: 3px solid #3b2a2e; border-radius: 50%; background: #fffdf8; color: #3b2a2e; box-shadow: 0 3px 10px rgb(59 42 46 / 0.22); cursor: pointer; transition: transform 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-turn:hover { background: #fff6dc; } .ds-turn:active { transform: translateY(2px) scale(0.96); } .ds-turn:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid #f2b233; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-turn svg { width: 26px; height: 26px; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 2.6; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }

components.name: Key Hint Chip
components.description: Printed-card chip naming keyboard controls; desktop only, not interactive.
components.css: .ds-keychip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 6px 12px; background: #fffdf8; color: #3b2a2e; border: 3px solid #3b2a2e; border-radius: 10px; box-shadow: 0 3px 10px rgb(59 42 46 / 0.22); font: 800 14px/1 'Nunito', sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-keychip kbd { font: 400 17px/1 'Lilita One', sans-serif; color: #2f5fa8; }

narrative.overview:
The kingdom is a paper stage. The papercraft diorama town is the stage floor and owns the whole window; the interface is theatre trim around its edges. M0 builds the first of that trim: a curtain-red pelmet with a scalloped hem across the top, carrying the kingdom's name and its numbers, and small white printed-card pieces (camera buttons, key hints, a fallback notice) resting on the stage. Everything, chrome and world alike, reads as printed card stock: flat hand-coloured fills, one dark ink outline, and soft paper shadows.

The feel is bright, warm and readable: a storybook kingdom made of simple shapes. Density is low; the town comes first and the chrome second. Big numerals over tiny capital labels let the player read their day at a glance. The world refuses the category default of parchment scrolls in carved wood frames; the wood here is a toy stage's base and floorboards, not ornament.

The diorama sits on an ink-edged wooden board (base wood) standing on a plank stage floor, lit by a white sun with real soft shadows over a pale sky. Grass carries a faint tile grid and fixed-seed tufts, so the board looks the same on every load.
keyCharacteristics: One ink colour outlines everything, in the UI and in the 3D world.
Flat fills only; colour changes are hard edges, never blends.
Marigold means "what you are doing right now" and nothing else.
Display numerals in a heavy rounded playbill face; body in a rounded workhorse.
Theatre trim stays on the edges of the stage; the map is never boxed in.
Keyboard first, with a visible marigold focus on everything focusable.

rules.name: The Right Now Rule
rules.body: Marigold (#f2b233) marks only what the player is doing right now: keyboard focus, the placement ghost, the chosen route. If an element is marigold while idle, it is wrong.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink (#3b2a2e) is the only outline colour, for the UI and the world. No grey borders, no coloured strokes, no second ink.

rules.name: The Flat Fill Rule
rules.body: Fills are flat. Where CSS gradients appear (the meter halves, the scallops) they are hard stops used to draw shapes, never blends. No soft colour gradients anywhere.

rules.name: The Big Number, Tiny Label Rule
rules.body: Top-bar readouts are large display numerals over a tiny uppercase label. The label names the column once; it is never repeated per row.

rules.name: The Stage Owns the Screen Rule
rules.body: Chrome lives on the edges; the town is never boxed in or covered by a frame.

rules.name: The Soft Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft and ink-tinted only. No hard offset block shadows.

dos: Do outline every UI piece and world edge in ink (#3b2a2e): 3px in the UI, 3.5px in the world.
Do keep marigold (#f2b233) for what the player is doing right now: focus, placement ghost, chosen route.
Do give every focusable element a visible 4px marigold focus outline.
Do set stat labels in blush (#fff2f4) on curtain red (#c8324a), as tiny tracked caps over big numerals.
Do use the single paper-lift shadow (0 3px 10px rgb(59 42 46 / 0.22)) for floating card pieces.
Do check every layout at 844x390 landscape.
Do keep camera turning a PC extra, hidden on coarse pointers.
Do keep theatre trim on the edges of the stage and in story moments.
donts: Don't use marigold as decoration, brand accent or idle fill.
Don't introduce a second outline colour or grey borders.
Don't blend gradients; colour changes are hard edges.
Don't use hard offset block shadows.
Don't put theatre trim inside lists.
Don't reach for parchment scrolls or carved wood frames.
